Your gas valve closes itself when the ground starts to shake.

Automatic gas shut-off valves that protect your home during an earthquake. Press the button to see what happens.

Call (844) 212-9186

Gas flowing. Valve open.

What happens in the first few seconds

  1. 1

    It senses the shaking

    A motion-triggered mechanism reacts to strong ground movement automatically.

  2. 2

    It closes the gas line

    The valve shuts on its own, before a damaged pipe or appliance connection can leak gas.

  3. 3

    It stays shut until you reset it

    Once you've checked for leaks, you reset the valve. We show you how at install.

Questions we hear

Smell gas? Leave the building first, then call your gas utility or 911 from outside.

Does this shut off water too?

No. This valve controls natural gas only. If you also want a water shut-off, call us and we'll discuss options.

Do I need a permit?

Often, yes, and the rules differ by city. We tell you what yours requires before we start.

How do I turn the gas back on?

After a shut-off, check for gas smell first, then reset the valve as we showed you. If you smell gas at any point, leave the building and call your gas utility.

Will it fit my gas meter?

Most single-family homes work. We confirm the meter and pipe layout at the site visit.

Have a valve installed before you need one.

Call us today and we'll check your meter, explain your city's requirements and give you a written quote.
